title: Propensity-Score Matching
summary: A race-specific propensity-score analysis estimating associations between neighborhood poverty and birth outcomes in restricted-access vital-statistics data, with documented assumptions and sensitivity checks.
overview: This project estimates how neighborhood (census-tract) poverty relates to adverse birth outcomes, using a propensity-score design fit separately within each race and ethnicity group. It is a mentored analysis on restricted-access vital-statistics data, run in a secure computing environment, and is being packaged for a manuscript in preparation.
myRole: I designed and implemented the analytic workflow end to end: race-specific propensity-score models, matching and balance diagnostics, outcome models, and sensitivity analyses, with documented assumptions and reproducible code.

sections.title: Design & Methods
content: Estimated race-specific propensity-score models with stratum-varying covariates, so matching reflects the covariate structure within each group.
Used matching as the primary approach, with overlap weighting and inverse-probability weighting as comparators, and assessed covariate balance in every stratum.
Fit outcome models with generalized estimating equations and empirical (sandwich) variance, reporting a complete-case primary analysis alongside a sensitivity analysis.

sections.title: Rigor & Reproducibility
content: Worked within the constraints of a secure, restricted-data environment, with a disk-frugal pipeline and per-output persistence.
Documented assumptions, exclusions, and analytic decisions to support transparent, reviewable results.
Coordinated with a faculty mentor toward a manuscript in preparation.

outcomes: Built a reproducible race-stratified propensity-score pipeline that achieves adequate covariate balance across strata.
Produced a complete-case primary analysis with a sensitivity analysis and documented assumptions.
Packaged methods and results toward a manuscript in preparation.
